text: A photonic-crystal slow-light waveguide with slowdown factor S = c/vg promises nonlinear enhancement scaling as S^2. Why is the realized benefit much smaller than S^2 in practical devices?
choices: The group velocity actually increases near the band edge
Slow light functions only in vacuum
The S enhancement applies only to linear absorption
Disorder-induced backscattering loss also scales as S^2, largely canceling the gain
explanation: Fabrication disorder produces backscattering loss that grows as S^2, offsetting the S^2 nonlinear enhancement, so real devices operate only at S ~ 10-30. The group velocity decreases (not increases) near the band edge, slow light is a guided-mode effect rather than a vacuum one, and the S^2 boost applies to the nonlinear interaction, not linear absorption alone.
